key_insight: Across binary main-group metal oxides, oxygen vacancy formation energies largely track cation reducibility and can be predicted using just crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property predictions could accelerate oxide screening for energy technologies, although solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Surveyed 39 oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to identify reconstructed neutral oxygen vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using crystal reduction potential and band gap.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Predictions may be less reliable where defect electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
